findings.title: OptimizedImage.downsize redefined from 4-arg to 3-arg form, silently breaking existing callers
findings.body: The class method `OptimizedImage.downsize` is now defined twice in the same class. The second definition (`def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149) replaces the first one (`def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145), so the 4-argument form is gone. Any other caller in the codebase that still does `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, 800, 600)` (a 4-arg call with separate width/height integers) will now either raise ArgumentError or, worse, have its 4th argument silently bound to `opts` while `800` becomes the dimensions string, producing nonsensical ImageMagick commands like `-resize 800x`. This is a hidden API break in a helper that is used by thumbnail jobs and other places; the new signature should be a new method name (e.g. `downsize_to`) and the old 4-arg form should be preserved or deprecated explicitly.

findings.title: 5 downsize iterations are mathematically insufficient for the feature to work
findings.body: Each pass uses `"80%"` dimensions, which shrinks image area to 0.8² = 0.64 of the original, so the file size drops by roughly 36% per iteration. After 5 iterations the file is approximately 0.64⁵ ≈ 33% of the original. With the default `max_image_size_kb` of 10MB, any source image above ~30MB cannot be brought under the limit in 5 passes; for example a 50MB image ends up at ~16MB and a 100MB image at ~33MB. The `while` loop then exits and `Upload.create_for` is invoked with an oversized file, so the 'auto-downsize' feature silently fails for any but moderately large images. Either the iteration count must scale with the initial size, the reduction factor must be more aggressive, or the loop should compute the required scale per iteration and pass it to `OptimizedImage.downsize`.

findings.title: Client upload size cap hardcoded to 10MB, bypassing the site setting
findings.body: `validateUploadedFile` previously read the cap from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, supporting independent `max_image_size_kb` and `max_attachment_size_kb`. It is now hardcoded to `10 * 1024` for every type. Consequences: (1) administrators lose the ability to tighten or loosen the client-side cap; (2) when an admin sets `max_image_size_kb` lower than 10MB the client still accepts up to 10MB and the user only finds out the upload is too large after the round trip; (3) the previous per-type distinction between images and attachments is lost. The site setting should still drive this value, or at minimum the hardcoded constant should be derived from the setting.

findings.title: 413 error message shows hardcoded 10MB instead of configured limit
findings.body: The 413 branch of `displayErrorForUpload` previously displayed `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` in the user-facing `file_too_large` error. It now uses a hardcoded `10 * 1024`, so the size quoted in the error dialog no longer matches the actual configured `max_image_size_kb`. Users will see '10MB' even when the real limit is 2MB or 50MB, leading to confusing UX after any admin change to the site setting.

findings.title: In-place downsize overwrites source file and ignores failure
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` reads from and writes to the same path. If the convert/gifsicle invocation fails (corrupt input, OOM, signal, bad permissions), ImageMagick may truncate or zero out the file before erroring, and the loop never checks the return value (`OptimizedImage.downsize` returns true/false), so the next iteration or the subsequent `Upload.create_for` will run on a corrupted/empty file. The fix is to write to a separate temp path, verify the result, then atomically rename, and to break out of the loop when downsize reports failure rather than blindly iterating again.

findings.title: URL download cap is a hardcoded 10MB, no longer tied to max_image_size_kb
findings.body: `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` replaces the previous cap of `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`. When an admin raises `max_image_size_kb` above 10MB (e.g. 50MB), the URL fetch path will now reject with a download error for any source between 10MB and the configured limit, even though the upload is supposed to be allowed and auto-downsized. Conversely, when the admin lowers `max_image_size_kb` to e.g. 1MB, the download limit is 10x the upload limit, which is intentional for downsizing but is not surfaced as a setting. The download cap should be a separate, larger setting (or derived as `max_image_size_kb * N`) rather than a hardcoded 10MB.

findings.title: OptimizedImage.optimize arity changed from 6 to 5
findings.body: `def self.optimize(operation, from, to, width, height, opts={})` (5 positional args + opts) is replaced by `def self.optimize(operation, from, to, dimensions, opts={})` (4 positional args + opts). Although this method is more internal than `downsize`, it is still a public class method, and any external caller (e.g. plugins or specs) passing separate width/height integers will now get those values joined as `"800600"` and passed to ImageMagick, which is silently wrong. The arity change should be paired with explicit deprecation or a new method name to avoid silent breakage.
